# CS 34.1 — Fuel venting

> [!summary]
> CS 34.1 is one sentence. It requires the aircraft to be designed to comply
> with the fuel venting requirements specified in point 21.A.21 of Part 21. It
> states no venting limit, no condition and no test of its own. The chain it
> opens runs through Part 21 and ends at the SARPs in ICAO Annex 16. CS-34 was
> repealed in May 2025, weeks after CS-E Amendment 8 was issued, and the repeal
> decision explains why the paragraph never carried content.

## Requirement

| Ref | Obligation | Strength |
|---|---|---|
| — | Design the aircraft to comply with the applicable fuel venting requirements as specified in point 21.A.21 of Annex I (Part 21) to Commission Regulation (EU) No 748/2012. | Required |
| **GM1 34.1** | Point 21.A.21 does not list the applicable requirements. It refers to point 21.A.20, which asks the applicant to demonstrate compliance with the environmental protection requirements designated by the Agency in accordance with point 21.B.85. The requirements are therefore in point 21.B.85. | Statement |

CS 34.1 addresses the **aircraft**, not the engine. Its sibling [[CS 34.2]]
addresses the aircraft engine. The difference decides which limb of
[[CS-E 1010]] operates.

### The chain, link by link

Each link is a reference out of the document before it. None of them states a
venting limit.

1. CS 34.1 sends the applicant to point 21.A.21 [ext CS 34.1].
2. Point 21.A.21(a)(2) requires the applicant to "demonstrate compliance in
   accordance with point 21.A.20" [ext 21.A.21(a)(2)].
3. Point 21.A.20(a) requires the applicant to demonstrate compliance with the
   environmental protection requirements "as established and notified to the
   applicant by the Agency in accordance with points 21.B.80, 21.B.82, 21.B.85"
   [ext 21.A.20(a)].
4. Point 21.B.85(a) makes that designation the Agency's act: for an engine type
   certificate, "the Agency shall designate and notify to the applicant the
   applicable environmental protection requirements from the essential
   requirements referred to in the first subparagraph of Article 9(2) of
   Regulation (EU) 2018/1139" [ext 21.B.85(a)].
5. GM2 21.B.85 names them: "The applicable environmental protection requirements
   are the Standards and Recommended Practices (SARPs) in Volume I, Volume II and
   Volume III of Annex 16 to the Chicago Convention ('ICAO Annex 16') for
   aircraft and engines for which the first subparagraph of Article 9(2) of
   Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 applies" [ext GM2 21.B.85].
6. For fuel venting the relevant part is Volume II Part II, which "applies to
   turbine engine powered aircraft manufactured after 18 February 1982"
   [ext GM1 21.B.85(a)].

**The vault records this chain and stops at step 6.** ICAO Annex 16 is not an
EASA document and this is a CS-E vault. The applicant follows the last link.

### The repeal

ED Decision 2025/005/R repealed CS-34, CS-36 and CS-CO2. EASA's publication
listing dates the repeal 27 May 2025; the decision's explanatory note carries no
issue date in its own text, and the file was created on 26 May 2025. The day is
therefore recorded from the listing, not from the document. CS-E
Amendment 8 was issued in April 2025 and still cites CS-34 throughout Subpart F.

The decision's own assessment is that the repealed specifications held no
requirements. CS-34 as last amended, together with CS-36 and CS-CO2, "only refer
to the requirements in Annex I (Part 21) to Commission Regulation (EU)
No 748/2012 for the issuance of a type certificate or a restricted type
certificate" [ext ED Decision 2025/005/R]. The stated objective is "to prevent
the future use of and reference to CS-34, CS-36 and CS-CO2 and any potential
confusion with the applicable environmental protection requirements"
[ext ED Decision 2025/005/R].

The repeal therefore removes a signpost, not an obligation. The chain above is
unchanged by it: it ran to Part 21 and ICAO Annex 16 before the repeal and runs
there now, with the first link deleted.

## Bearing on this engine

[[CS-E 1010]] requires the engine to be designed to comply with the fuel venting
specifications of CS 34.1, and, where those specifications are directed at the
aircraft, to carry provisions that let the aircraft comply. CS 34.1 is directed
at the aircraft in its entirety. **The second limb of CS-E 1010 is therefore the
operative one for this engine**, and the deliverable is installation
information rather than an engine limit.

Fuel venting is not restricted by engine type. Volume II Part II reaches turbine
engine powered aircraft, so a turboshaft installation is inside it
[ext GM1 21.B.85(a)]. This is the opposite of the emissions case in
[[CS 34.2]].

The repeal does not release the applicant. The requirements were never in CS-34,
and point 21.B.85 designates them whether or not CS-E names CS-34.

[VERIFY: which amendment level of ICAO Annex 16 Volume II the Agency designates
for this certification. GM2 21.B.85 carries a correspondence table between the
amendment levels and the EU regulations that implemented them; the table is
outside the scope this vault records, and the designation is the Agency's act
under point 21.B.85(a).]
